attributes.description: Alerts when the proportion of lambda/edge invocations that crash before returning any HTTP response (http.response.status_code == -1) exceeds 1% over a 15-minute window. These hard failures are excluded from standard HTTP error-rate calculations but represent the most severe class of runtime defect.
attributes.name: [Vercel OTel] Lambda/edge function crash rate elevated

investigation_guide.blob:
## Lambda/Edge Crash Rate Elevated

### Triage Steps
1. `http.response.status_code == -1` means the function crashed (unhandled exception, timeout, or OOM) before any response was returned to the client — this is a hard failure, worse than a handled 5xx.
2. Inspect stderr output for crashing invocations: `FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default | WHERE vercel.log.source == "<source>" AND http.response.status_code == -1 | KEEP @timestamp, message, http.route, deployment.id, vercel.execution.region | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 50`
3. Correlate with `deployment.id` — a spike immediately after a new deployment strongly suggests a rollback is needed.
4. Check for timeout patterns (crashes with no stderr message) versus explicit exceptions (stderr present) — timeouts may indicate a downstream dependency (database, third-party API) is slow or unavailable.

### Escalation
Treat this as higher severity than the standard 5xx error-rate rule — a crash means the request received no response at all, not even an error page. Page the on-call engineer if the crash rate exceeds 5%.

esqlQuery.esql:
FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default
| WHERE deployment.environment.name == "production"
    AND vercel.log.source IN ("lambda", "edge")
| STATS
    total = COUNT(*),
    crashes = COUNT(*) WHERE http.response.status_code == -1
  BY vercel.log.source
// Minimum sample size to avoid noisy alerts on low-traffic sources
| WHERE total > 20
| EVAL crash_rate_pct = ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(crashes) / total * 100.0, 2)
// Alert threshold: crashes are rarer and more severe than generic 5xx responses, so this is set tighter.
// Adjust based on your application's tolerance for cold-start/timeout-driven crashes.
| WHERE crash_rate_pct > 1.0
| SORT crash_rate_pct DESC
| LIMIT 10
